scenes: Six point three billion dollars left Binance in one night. It started with a job interview.
In June, a Binance wallet developer downloaded a fake copy of a tool. It came from an ad, placed above the real one in search results.
In September, another engineer, looking for a new job, had a video interview with the CEO of a company that did not exist. Then downloaded its code.
On October twentieth, the hackers used those two computers to take over the wallet developers' systems.
On October twenty-ninth, they ran one script. Two hundred thirty-three million X R P left five hot wallets in four minutes. Then bitcoin, and more.
Most of it was gone in about twenty minutes. Binance froze about two point eight five billion dollars.
The F B I blames North Korean hackers. And it all started with a job interview.
